fixed.what: realProc's three PowerShell texts now start with $ErrorActionPreference='Stop' (shared PS_PREFIX), so a failed CIM query exits non-zero: alive and boot return null and list throws proc-unavailable 2. alive() now maps its output through the new exported pure function aliveFromQuery: only 'NONE' means dead, and any output that is not NONE, NOSTART or an ISO time is null (unknown). The texts are exported read-only as PS_SCRIPTS.
fixed.test_added: T36m (pure: every PS_SCRIPTS text starts with the Stop preference); T89b (one real PowerShell per text, Get-CimInstance shadowed by a function that writes a non-terminating error: the alive and list texts must exit non-zero and never print NONE). Against the unfixed text T89b failed with 'alive: exited 0 with stdout NONE', which is the reviewer's reproduction.

fixed.what: realProc.alive compares one-sidedly via aliveFromQuery: the listed process is the holder iff its CreationDate <= the recorded start + START_TOLERANCE_MS. A slow start-up no longer reads as dead; a pid reused by a later process is still told apart. sameStartTime itself is unchanged (other scripts use it).
fixed.test_added: T36l (aliveFromQuery cases: 12 s of start-up is alive, created 2.5 s after the recorded start is pid reuse, junk output is null). It fails against the symmetric comparison. T85's existing asserts (+1 s true, -5 s false, '2000-...' false) still pass.

fixed.what: acquireLock judges a holder only once its lock bytes have stayed unchanged for min(LOCK_JUDGE_AFTER=50, retries) consecutive sightings, counted by the retry loop with no clock read. Ordinary contention therefore starts no PowerShell. A caller with fewer retries still judges at its last retry, so T29/T30 with retries 2-3 keep their behaviour. breakStale re-reads the lock right before the rename and skips the break ('changed') when the bytes differ from the ones judged. readLockRecord now also returns the raw bytes.
fixed.test_added: T36g (with retries 60, alive is called once, at sighting 51); T36h (a lock whose bytes change on every read is never judged: alive is called 0 times, lock-busy 75); T36i (a lock replaced between the judgement and the break is never renamed). All three fail against the old loop.

fixed.what: A lock file that is unreadable (empty or not a record) and byte-for-byte unchanged for the whole retry budget is broken when retries >= LOCK_UNREADABLE_MIN_RETRIES (50; scripts pass 300, about 30 s). The break uses the same protocol: pre-rename re-read, rename, compare bytes, create with wx, otherwise restore by link. No process query is made. The lock-break line keeps the contract shape stale {pid,start_time,nonce,script}, all null here, and adds data.unreadable {bytes: length, sha256}. With fewer retries the lock stays, as before (lock-busy 75).
fixed.test_added: T36j (empty and truncated-JSON locks: with retries 3 the lock stays; with retries 50 it is broken, with no process query and a lock-break line with null stale and unreadable bytes and sha256); T36k (a guard: an unreadable lock that becomes a live record during the budget is not broken). T36j fails against the old code.

fixed.what: No library change was needed: the guards at appendLedger (before writeLedgerLine) and writeTasks (before writeAtomic) were already there, but untested.
fixed.test_added: T42b (the run.lock nonce is swapped when tailInfo opens ledger.jsonl: lock-lost 75 and the ledger bytes are unchanged); T50b (the run.lock nonce is swapped when writeTasks reads tasks.json: lock-lost 75, tasks.json and .prev unchanged). Both fail with the respective assertHeld replaced by void 0 (mutation M11 and its writeTasks twin).

fixed.what: T21 (reader in another process) now wraps the 200 writes in try/finally. The finally always writes the stop file, waits up to 10 s for the reader (the timer is cleared), and kills the reader only if it is still running. No child is left when writeAtomic throws.
fixed.test_added: None separate: this was a fix to the test itself. T21 still passes (2.6 s).

fixed.what: Fixed in lib, without a schema change. wordCount splits on whitespace and on Unicode format characters, category Cf (U+200B, U+2060, ...), and counts every Han, Hiragana or Katakana character as a word. The x-maxWords validator also refuses strings longer than x-maxWords * MAX_CODEPOINTS_PER_WORD (40) code points, reported under keyword x-maxWords. card.schema.json is unchanged (no maxLength added), so no file format changed.
fixed.test_added: T67b (500 tokens joined by U+200B or U+2060, 16 Han or Hiragana characters, and a 601-code-point token are refused; 15 Han characters and a 600-code-point token pass; ordinary counts unchanged). It fails against the old wordCount. T67 still passes.

not_fixed.why: The reviewer's 'at the least, report a lock-unreadable anomaly in status' is status.mjs, which is not my file. The library now breaks such a lock after a full retry budget, so it no longer blocks forever. A status anomaly would still help while the lock waits; this is a request to the status.mjs owner.

A backward wall-clock step of more than 2 s between the holder's creation and its own start-time reading still makes a live holder look like a later process. The one-sided rule cannot tell this from pid reuse without a different record format, and a format change was ruled out.

tests.command: node tools/lane.mjs --label lib-fix --timeout-s 300 -- node --test --test-concurrency=1 tcb/test/lib.test.mjs (cwd tcb-build)
tests.output_tail: tests 190, pass 188, fail 0, cancelled 0, skipped 2 (T82, T92 needs-app), duration_ms 79958. Mutation check (lane label lib-fix-mut): with all eight fixes reverted together (assertHeld in appendLedger and in writeTasks, Stop preference, one-sided compare, judge-after count, pre-rename re-read, unreadable break, wordCount and length cap), T36g, T36h, T36i, T36j, T36l, T36m, T42b, T50b, T67b and T89b fail (10 of 10); the guard T36k passes on both. lib.mjs was restored and checked byte-identical to the fixed copy (tmp/lib.mjs.fixed).

lib_change_requests: Other files (not mine): status.mjs:129/627 and handover.mjs:131 judge holders with lib.sameStartTime, which is symmetric. They should use lib.aliveFromQuery semantics (listed start <= recorded + tolerance) for the same reason as LR-2.
Other files (not mine): status.mjs could report an unreadable run.lock or watcher.lock as an anomaly (LR-4).

Other files (not mine): commit.mjs:370 uses lib.wordCount for index summaries; it now also splits on Unicode format characters (category Cf) and counts CJK characters as words. Rerun the commit tests. Every schema with x-maxWords also gets the 40-code-points-per-word length bound; rerun the tests of scripts that validate cards, fmea, hazards, review, sentence and stpa.
